summary: A stack removes the newest item first (LIFO). A queue removes the oldest item first (FIFO). Java's ArrayDeque does both jobs.
notes: Declare the stack as Deque<Character> to get push() and pop(). Declare the queue as Queue<String> to get offer() and poll().
stack.isEmpty() is checked first, so pop() never runs on an empty stack. .equals() compares the two Character objects by value.
poll() returns null on an empty queue instead of throwing. remove() throws NoSuchElementException.
pitfall: Calling pop() on an empty ArrayDeque throws NoSuchElementException. Check stack.isEmpty() first. The old Stack class also works but is slower, so prefer ArrayDeque.
